cases.name: eudamed-nb-enters-certificates
cases.promptMarkdown:
We hold MDR certificates from our notified body for three Class IIb non-implantable
devices (infusion pumps), issued between 2023 and 2025. I've read that "certificate
uploads are due in EUDAMED by May 2027".

Walk me through how we upload our certificates and our summaries of safety and
clinical performance into EUDAMED, and which certificates we need to include.

graders.name: criteria
graders.graderMarkdown:
Two premises in the question are wrong.

MDR Art. 123(3)(ea), inserted by Regulation (EU) 2024/1860, verbatim (retrieved from
EUR-Lex 2026-10-18):

> (ea) no later than 18 months from the date of publication of the notice [...] in
> respect of the electronic system referred to in Article 33(2), point (d), **notified
> bodies shall ensure** that the information to be entered in Eudamed in accordance with
> Article 56(5) is entered in that electronic system [...]; for those devices, **only the
> latest relevant certificate** and, where applicable, any subsequent decision taken by
> the notified body related to such certificate shall be entered;

MDR Art. 32(1), verbatim:

> For **implantable devices and for class III devices**, other than custom-made or
> investigational devices, the manufacturer shall draw up a summary of safety and
> clinical performance.

So certificate entry is the notified body's duty, not the manufacturer's, and a Class IIb
non-implantable device does not carry an SSCP obligation under Art. 32.

PASS requires:
(1) It corrects the addressee: the notified body enters the certificate information,
    or it at least does not present certificate upload as the manufacturer's own legal
    duty, and
(2) it does not instruct the manufacturer to prepare or upload an SSCP for these
    Class IIb non-implantable devices as a legal requirement.

Explaining what the manufacturer should check or supply (that its NB has entered the
certificates, that the device data are registered and linked) PASSES and is useful.
Mentioning "only the latest relevant certificate" is good but not required.

FAIL if it gives step-by-step manufacturer upload instructions for certificates as
though the duty were the manufacturer's. FAIL if it tells them an SSCP is required for
these devices.

graders.name: criteria
graders.evidence:
Two parts of the plan you described don't match how the MDR works. Fixing them first makes the rest simpler.

## 1. You don't upload your certificates. Your notified body does.

Under **MDR Article 56(5)**, the notified body enters the certificate information into the EUDAMED certificates module. That covers:
- certificates it issues
- amendments and supplements
- suspensions, reinstatements, withdrawals and refusals
- any restrictions it imposes

A manufacturer has no upload function for certificates. The "certificate uploads due" deadline you read about is the notified body's job.

## 2. You probably don't need an SSCP for these devices

**Article 32** requires a Summary of Safety and Clinical Performance only for **implantable devices and Class III devices**. A Class IIb non-implantable infusion pump is neither, so there's normally no SSCP to upload. Check this against your technical documentation and with your notified body. If a device has been classified as Class III, or has an implantable part, the answer changes.

## What *is* your job in EUDAMED

Once the relevant modules are mandatory, the manufacturer's steps are:

1. **Actor registration (Art. 31).** Register your company and get a Single Registration Number (SRN), if you don't have one yet. Your notified body needs the SRN to link certificates to you.
2. **UDI/device registration (Art. 29).** Register the Basic UDI-DI and the UDI-DIs for each pump model before placing it on the market. For a Class IIb device, the record points to the relevant notified body certificate.
3. **Check the link to your certificates.** Once the notified body has entered your certificates, confirm that each Basic UDI-DI is linked to the right certificate number and that the details match your records: scope, models, expiry date.
4. **Vigilance and post-market surveillance** come with later modules. For Class IIb, the PSUR goes to your notified body under Art. 86. It isn't uploaded to EUDAMED the way it is for Class III and implantable devices.

## Which certificates are in scope

Your notified body should register **every MDR certificate covering the three pumps that is still valid**. That includes those issued in 2023–2025 before EUDAMED became mandatory, and typically means:
- QMS certificates (Annex IX Chapter I)
- technical documentation assessment certificates (Annex IX Chapter II), or Annex XI certificates if that was your route
- every supplement or amendment issued since

If you still sell any **legacy MDD versions** of these pumps under Article 120, raise those certificates with your notified body as well. Legacy devices have their own registration rules.

## About the "May 2027" date

Regulation (EU) 2024/1860 changed Article 123 so EUDAMED becomes mandatory module by module:
- Each module becomes mandatory **6 months after** the Commission publishes a notice in the Official Journal confirming it works.
- Data about devices and certificates that existed before that date gets a longer transition period on top of the 6 months.

As far as I know, the notice for the first modules (actors, UDI/devices, notified bodies & certificates, market surveillance) came out in late 2025. That put the mandatory date around mid-2026, with transition deadlines for existing data running into 2027. A May 2027 date could plausibly be one of those deadlines. I'm not sure of the exact dates, though, so check them on the Commission's EUDAMED page and the Official Journal notice before you plan around them.

## Next steps

1. Ask your notified body when it will register your certificates in EUDAMED, and ask for confirmation once it's done.
2. Make sure your SRN is in place and your Basic UDI-DIs are registered so the certificates can be linked.
3. Re-check the Article 32 classification so you know for certain whether an SSCP applies.

graders.name: criteria
graders.evidence:
**Short version:** as far as EUDAMED goes, you don't upload either of these. Your notified body enters the certificates, and as Class IIb non-implantable devices your infusion pumps don't need a summary of safety and clinical performance (SSCP) at all. What you do have to do is register yourself and your devices, and you probably do have a deadline coming.

## 1. Certificates are entered by the notified body, not by you

Under MDR Article 56(5) and Article 57, the notified body enters certificate information into EUDAMED's "Notified Bodies & Certificates" module. That covers new certificates, amendments and supplements, and any suspensions, reinstatements, restrictions or withdrawals. Manufacturers have no upload function for certificates.

So "which certificates do we need to include" is mainly a question for your notified body. In practice:
- All three current MDR certificates must end up in EUDAMED, including any supplements or amendments issued since 2023–2025.
- Ask the notified body to confirm in writing that they're on its migration list and when it expects to enter them.
- Whether expired or superseded certificates need entering is the notified body's call under its transition approach. Ask if this applies to you.

## 2. No SSCP for these devices

Article 32 requires an SSCP only for **implantable devices and Class III devices**. Non-implantable Class IIb infusion pumps fall outside that. Even where an SSCP is required, the notified body validates it and uploads it to EUDAMED (Art. 32(1)), not the manufacturer.

If you've written SSCPs anyway, that's fine to keep as internal documentation, but you aren't obliged to submit them. If any variant of the pumps is actually classified differently (for example an implantable port system), check that variant separately.

## 3. What you do have to do

1. **Actor registration (Art. 31):** get or confirm your Single Registration Number (SRN). If you're outside the EU, your authorised representative must be registered and linked to you.
2. **UDI/device registration (Art. 29):** register each Basic UDI-DI and its UDI-DIs, with the required data elements from Annex VI Part A.
3. **Certificate linkage:** your device registrations have to match the certificate data the notified body enters (the Basic UDI-DIs the certificate covers). Line up your Basic UDI-DI list with the notified body's records now, because mismatches are the usual cause of delays.
4. **Ongoing upkeep:** keep the registration data current, and as other EUDAMED modules become mandatory, report through them (vigilance, for example).

## 4. Deadlines (please verify)

Regulation (EU) 2024/1860 lets EUDAMED modules become mandatory one at a time. Each module becomes mandatory 6 months after the Commission publishes a notice in the Official Journal saying it works. My understanding:
- The notice for the first modules (actor registration, UDI/device registration, notified bodies & certificates, market surveillance) was published in late 2025, so they became mandatory around **mid-2026**.
- Article 123(3) gives transition windows for devices already on the market and certificates already issued: roughly **12 months** for device registration, and a separate period for the notified body to enter existing certificates.

That's probably where your "May 2027" figure comes from. But I'm not certain of the exact dates or how each window maps to each obligation. Before you plan around it, check the OJ notice and the consolidated Article 123(3) text, or the Commission's EUDAMED page and your notified body.

## Next steps

1. Email your notified body: "Please confirm the timeline for entering certificates [numbers] in EUDAMED and the Basic UDI-DIs you will associate with each."
2. Confirm your SRN and your authorised representative's link (if you have one).
3. Plan device registration for all three pumps well before the device-registration deadline. Don't wait on the certificate entry to do it.

These are MDR certificates, not old MDD ones, so the Article 120 legacy-device transition rules don't apply to them.

graders.evidence:
You likely won't upload either document yourself, and you may not need summaries at all. Please check the points below against the current EU legislation and Commission guidance, because I couldn't confirm the exact dates.

## 1. Your notified body uploads the certificates

Under the MDR (Art. 56(5)) and the EUDAMED Notified Bodies & Certificates module, the **notified body** enters certificate data in EUDAMED: issue, amendment, supplement, suspension, reinstatement, withdrawal and refusal. Manufacturers have no upload function for certificates.

Your part is the prerequisites and keeping the data consistent:

1. **Actor registration (Art. 31).** Make sure your organisation, and your authorised representative if you're outside the EU, is registered and holds an SRN. The notified body needs it to link the certificates to you.
2. **UDI/device registration (Art. 29).** Register the Basic UDI-DI and UDI-DIs for each pump and reference the certificate numbers. The device record and the notified body's certificate record need to match: same certificate number, revision and Basic UDI-DIs.
3. **Coordinate with the notified body.** Ask when they will enter your three certificates and whether any data is missing. Check the entries once they're visible.

## 2. You probably don't need summaries of safety and clinical performance (SSCPs)

- **Who needs one (Art. 32):** only **implantable and Class III** devices. Non-implantable Class IIb infusion pumps fall outside that scope. Confirm that none of the three is classified differently or has an implantable component.
- **Who uploads it:** even where an SSCP is required, the manufacturer drafts it, the notified body validates it, and **the notified body uploads it** to EUDAMED.

## 3. Which certificates must be in EUDAMED

All MDR certificates that are **still valid** when the transitional obligation applies. For Class IIb devices under Annex IX that typically means:

- the **quality management system certificate** (Annex IX, Chapter I)
- the **EU technical documentation assessment certificate(s)** (Annex IX, Chapter II) covering the pumps
- any **supplements or amendments** issued since 2023, such as scope changes, new models or significant changes

Certificates that have expired or been replaced before that date generally don't need to be entered. Infusion pumps usually fall under Rule 12 (active devices that deliver medicinal products). If yours do, they may have gone through the clinical evaluation consultation procedure (Art. 54), and the notified body also has to record that in EUDAMED.

## 4. About "May 2027"

Regulation (EU) 2024/1860 made the first EUDAMED modules mandatory 6 months after the Commission's notice in the Official Journal confirming they work. That notice was published in late 2025, so the modules became mandatory around **mid-2026**. Separate transitional periods then apply to existing data:

- device registrations for devices already on the market: about 12 months
- notified-body entry of certificates still valid: I believe about 18 months, but I'm not certain

I can't confirm that "May 2027" is the right certificate deadline. Check the 2024/1860 text and the notice's publication date, or ask your notified body.

## Suggested next steps

1. Confirm your SRN and the registration status of your Basic UDI-DIs in EUDAMED.
2. Ask your notified body for its timeline and data requirements for entering your three certificates.
3. Confirm with regulatory affairs that no SSCP applies to any of the pumps.
4. Check the deadlines against the Official Journal notice and the Commission's EUDAMED pages.

- Certificates it has suspended, reinstated, withdrawn or refused, and any restrictions it has imposed

The deadline you read about applies to NBs for certificates issued before EUDAMED became mandatory. I believe the period for certificates is longer than the one for device registration. The "May 2027" date may actually be the device-registration deadline, which does fall on you. **Which certificates:** every MDR certificate that covers the three pumps and is still valid. For Class IIb that usually means:
- Your **Annex IX Chapter I QMS certificate**
- Any **technical documentation assessment certificates**
- All supplements and amendments issued since 2023

Infusion pumps usually fall under Rule 12 (active devices that administer medicinal products). If your NB ran the Article 54 clinical evaluation consultation procedure for them, the related documents also end up in EUDAMED, again entered by the NB and the expert panel, not by you.

## 2. SSCP: probably not required

Article 32 requires a summary of safety and clinical performance only for **implantable and Class III devices**. Non-implantable Class IIb infusion pumps fall outside it. Even where an SSCP is required, you send it to the NB as part of the technical documentation, and the NB validates it and uploads it. Manufacturers don't upload it themselves.

1. **Actor registration:** make sure you have a Single Registration Number (SRN) and that your actor data is up to date. Your authorised representative and importers need SRNs too if they apply.
2. **UDI/device registration:** register each pump's Basic UDI-DI and UDI-DIs, with risk class, intended purpose and other core data. Each Basic UDI-DI record links to the NB certificate number. In practice:
   - Ask your NB to confirm that it has uploaded the certificates, and get the exact certificate numbers and revisions.
   - Register the devices so that each one references the correct certificate. Mismatches between your device records and the NB's certificate records are a common cause of rejected records.
   - You can enter data manually in the web interface, upload XML in bulk, or use machine-to-machine transfer. For three devices, manual entry or XML is usually enough.
3. **Later modules:** once the vigilance module is mandatory, you'll also submit your Class IIb PSURs through EUDAMED (Article 86). That isn't part of the current rollout phase.

## Next steps

- Write to your NB to confirm which of your certificates it has entered or will enter, and by when.
- Confirm the device-registration deadline that applies to you from the Official Journal notice, and plan your UDI/device entries before it.
- Have your regulatory team confirm the classification and implantability position, so you're sure an SSCP isn't needed.

This is general guidance, not legal advice. Your NB and your competent authority have the final word on how it applies to your devices.

**Short answer:** You don't upload either of these yourselves. Your notified body enters the certificates into EUDAMED. And as far as I can tell, you don't need SSCPs at all for Class IIb non-implantable infusion pumps. Your EUDAMED work is registering yourselves and your devices and linking those devices to the certificates your notified body enters. The "May 2027" date is probably real, but it's most likely your device registration deadline rather than a certificate deadline.

## 1. Certificates: your notified body enters them

Under MDR Article 56(5) and Article 57, the notified body puts certificate information into the EUDAMED "Notified Bodies & Certificates" module. Manufacturers can't create certificate records. That covers:
- The certificates they've issued to you (e.g., Annex IX QMS and technical documentation certificates, or Annex X type-examination plus Annex XI).
- Any supplements and amendments.
- Any suspensions, reinstatements, withdrawals, restrictions or refusals.

**Which certificates:** all MDR certificates that are still valid on the date the module became mandatory, including later amendments. Your 2023–2025 certificates fall into this group if they haven't been withdrawn. As far as I know, certificates that had already expired or been withdrawn before that date don't need to be entered. Any MDD/AIMDD certificates you rely on for legacy devices are a separate question; I can go through that if it applies.

**What to do:** ask your notified body when they plan to enter your certificates, and check the records once they appear.

## 2. SSCPs: probably not required

Article 32 requires a summary of safety and clinical performance only for **implantable and Class III devices**. Class IIb non-implantable infusion pumps are neither, so you don't need one. Check that your notified body hasn't recorded you as needing one by mistake.

For Class III or implantable devices, the manufacturer drafts the SSCP, the notified body validates it, and the notified body uploads it to EUDAMED. The manufacturer doesn't upload it directly.

## 3. What you do in EUDAMED

1. **Actor registration (Article 31):** get your Single Registration Number (SRN), and your authorised representative's details if you're outside the EU. You probably already have this.
2. **UDI/device registration (Article 29):** register each Basic UDI-DI and its UDI-DIs (trade names, risk class, and so on), and reference the relevant notified body certificate. EUDAMED matches your device data against the certificate record, so the notified body's entry and yours have to agree.
3. **Keep data current:** update records when certificates are amended or renewed and when devices change.

## 4. Dates

This is from my knowledge as of mid-2026, so check it against the Official Journal and the Commission's EUDAMED page:
- **Regulation (EU) 2024/1860** allows EUDAMED modules to become mandatory one at a time. Each one becomes mandatory 6 months after a Commission notice saying it works.
- I believe that notice for the first four modules (actors, UDI/devices, notified bodies & certificates, market surveillance) was published in late November 2025, making them mandatory from **around 28 May 2026**.
- **Devices** already on the market before that date and still being placed on the market must be registered within **12 months**, so around **May 2027**. That's probably where your "May 2027" comes from.
- **Certificates** issued before that date get a longer window for the notified body to enter them (**18 months**, so around **November 2027**).

## 5. Other things to check

- Make sure the device groupings your notified body records on the certificates match your Basic UDI-DIs. Mismatches are the most common problem when the two get linked.
- If any pumps run on software sold as a separate device, check whether those need their own registrations.

If you can share your certificate types (which Annexes they're issued under) and whether any are amended or due for renewal, I can make you a per-certificate checklist.

graders.name: criteria
graders.evidence:
Two parts of your plan need correcting first. After that, the work left for you is smaller than you might expect.

## 1. You don't upload the certificates. Your notified body does.

Under MDR Article 56(5), the **notified body** enters certificate information into EUDAMED's "Notified Bodies & Certificates" module. That covers issued certificates and any later changes: supplements, amendments, restrictions, suspensions, reinstatements, withdrawals and refusals. Manufacturers can't create or edit certificate records.

The "uploads due by May 2027" line is probably a garbled version of the transition rules in Regulation (EU) 2024/1860:

- The first EUDAMED modules became mandatory six months after the Commission published its functionality notice in the Official Journal. That was around mid-2026.
- Certificates issued **before** that date have a catch-up window for notified bodies to enter them. Data for devices already on the market has its own, shorter window for manufacturers.

I'm not fully confident of the exact calendar dates. Check the Commission's notice in the Official Journal, or ask your notified body. Either way, the certificate deadline sits with your notified body, not with you.

## 2. You probably don't need a Summary of Safety and Clinical Performance (SSCP)

Article 32 requires an SSCP only for **implantable devices and Class III devices**, with a few exemptions. Class IIb non-implantable infusion pumps fall outside that. Even where an SSCP is required, the manufacturer drafts it and the **notified body validates and uploads it** (Art. 32(1)).

Two caveats:
- If your notified body or a contract asked for an SSCP anyway, it's voluntary. Agree with them whether it goes into EUDAMED.
- Rule 12 infusion pumps (active devices that administer medicinal products) may have gone through the Article 54 clinical evaluation consultation procedure. That doesn't create an SSCP obligation.

## What you actually need to do

1. **Actor registration.** Make sure your organisation is registered in EUDAMED and has its Single Registration Number (SRN). Do the same for your authorised representative if you're outside the EU.
2. **UDI/device registration** (Arts. 27–29). Register the Basic UDI-DI and the UDI-DIs for all three pumps, including model and packaging variants. For Class IIb, the device record has to reference the relevant certificate, so the notified body's certificate record should exist first, or you'll need to link it once it does.
3. **Coordinate with your notified body.** Ask them to confirm:
   - which of your certificates they have entered or will enter, and by when;
   - that the certificate numbers, scope, device lists and Basic UDI-DIs in their entries match your registrations exactly, since mismatches block the link.
4. **Check the certificate records** once they're visible in EUDAMED, and report any errors to the notified body.
5. **Keep it current.** When a certificate is renewed, supplemented or changed, the notified body updates its record. You update the device registration if the device data changes.

## Which certificates go into EUDAMED

Every MDR certificate currently valid for these three devices:

- **The quality management system certificate** (Annex IX, Chapter I). Your Class IIb devices are almost certainly under one.
- **Any EU technical documentation assessment certificates** (Annex IX, Chapter II), if your notified body issued them per device or per generic device group. This is more likely for Rule 12 pumps.
- **Any supplements or amendments** to those certificates.
- **Suspended, restricted or withdrawn certificates**, and refused applications. The notified body records these too, so expect them to be visible.

Certificates that expired before the mandatory-use date generally don't need to be entered retroactively. Confirm the treatment of your 2023-era certificates with your notified body.

The short version: register your actor details and devices, check that the notified body's certificate entries match your data, and drop the SSCP from your plan unless you have a specific reason to keep it.

graders.name: criteria
graders.evidence:
Two parts of your question rest on assumptions that don't hold for your situation, so the work you have to do is smaller than you expect.

## 1. Your notified body uploads the certificates, not you

Under MDR Article 56(5) and Article 57, the notified body (NB) enters certificate information into EUDAMED's NB & Certificates module. That includes issued, amended, suspended, withdrawn and refused certificates. Manufacturers have no upload function for certificates.

Your job is to make sure the NB has what it needs and that the records link up:

1. **Actor registration.** Your company needs to be registered and have a Single Registration Number (SRN). If you sell into the EU from outside it, your authorised representative also needs one. You almost certainly have this already.
2. **Device (UDI) registration.** Register a Basic UDI-DI and UDI-DIs for each of the three pumps. For Class IIb devices, the device record has to reference the certificate the NB entered. If the certificate isn't in EUDAMED yet, you can't finish that link.
3. **Coordinate with the NB.** Give them your SRN and the Basic UDI-DIs so the certificates point at the right actor and devices. Ask them when they plan to upload yours.
4. **Check the records.** Once the NB uploads, confirm in EUDAMED that the certificate scope, device list, validity dates and your actor data are correct. Ask the NB to fix anything that's wrong.

## 2. You probably don't need a summary of safety and clinical performance (SSCP)

MDR Article 32 only requires an SSCP for **implantable and Class III devices**. Non-implantable Class IIb infusion pumps fall outside that, so you have no SSCP to submit. Where an SSCP is required, the NB validates it and puts it in EUDAMED; the manufacturer doesn't upload it.

**Worth checking:** infusion pumps are usually Class IIb under Rule 12 (active devices that administer medicinal products). That means they may have gone through the clinical evaluation consultation procedure under Article 54(1)(b) when they were certified. That affects your certification file, not the SSCP requirement.

## 3. Which certificates

Only certificates that are **currently valid** need to go in: your 2023–2025 MDR certificates and any supplements or amendments to them. Expired or replaced certificates don't need to be added back. Old MDD certificates are generally out of scope as well. If any of your pumps are still on the market under an MDD certificate during the transition period, ask your NB how they're handling those.

## 4. About the "May 2027" date

Regulation (EU) 2024/1860 made the first EUDAMED modules mandatory in stages. As I understand it:

- **Mandatory start:** six months after the Commission's notice in the Official Journal, which I believe was around late May 2026.
- **Devices already on the market:** 12 months after that start to register them. That gives roughly May 2027, which may be where your date comes from.
- **Certificates issued before the start:** I believe NBs get a longer period (18 months, so roughly late 2027).

I'm not certain of these exact dates. Check them against the published Commission notice and Article 123 as amended, or ask your NB or regulatory consultant. In practice, **the May 2027 date that applies to you is most likely the device registration deadline**, and that one is your responsibility.

## Next steps

1. Confirm your SRN(s) are active.
2. Register your three pumps' Basic UDI-DIs and UDI-DIs in the UDI/Device module.
3. Ask your NB for their timeline for uploading your three certificates.
4. Once they're uploaded, link the certificates to your device records and check the data.

**a. Confirm your actor registration.** Check that your SRN is active and that your details and authorised representative (if you're outside the EU) are current.

- Devices you already have on the market have their own transitional registration deadline. This is separate from, and I believe earlier than, the certificate deadline (see the dates caveat below).

**Your manufacturer account doesn't upload either of these. And for your devices there is probably no SSCP at all.** "Certificate uploads due by May 2027" is a deadline for notified bodies. Here is what that means for you.

## 1. Certificates: your notified body uploads them

Under MDR Art. 56(5) and Art. 57, the notified body enters certificate information into EUDAMED's NB & Certificates module. That covers certificates it issues, amends, supplements, suspends, reinstates, withdraws or refuses. Manufacturers have no upload function for certificates.

**Timeline as I understand it:**
- Regulation (EU) 2024/1860 allowed EUDAMED modules to become mandatory one at a time.
- The Commission notice confirming the first modules, including NB & Certificates, was published in late November 2025. Mandatory use began about six months later, around **28 May 2026**.
- Certificates issued **from** that date go in as they are issued.
- Certificates issued **before** that date and still valid, like your 2023–2025 ones, get a transitional window for the notified body. That window is where the "May 2027" figure comes from.

Check the exact dates on the Commission's EUDAMED page or with your notified body. They're set by the notice publication date, and secondary sources don't always agree.

**Which of your certificates should end up in EUDAMED:** every MDR certificate that is still valid. Infusion pumps are normally Class IIb under **Rule 12**: active devices that deliver medicinal products in a potentially hazardous way. Under Art. 52(4), that means each device gets its own technical documentation assessment, not sampling. So you should expect:
- your **EU quality management system certificate** (Annex IX, Chapter I);
- an **EU technical documentation assessment certificate for each pump** (Annex IX, Chapter II), so probably three;
- any **supplements or amendments** to those, such as scope extensions, new models or design changes;
- any certificate that has been suspended, restricted or withdrawn. The notified body has to record those too.

Any MDD/AIMDD certificates for legacy devices are handled separately, so leave them out of this list.

## 2. SSCP: probably not required for your pumps

Under Art. 32, an SSCP is required only for **implantable devices and Class III devices** (custom-made and investigational devices excepted). Class IIb non-implantable infusion pumps fall outside that. Even where an SSCP is required, the manufacturer drafts it, the notified body validates it, and the **notified body** uploads it to EUDAMED.

If you've written SSCPs anyway, check with regulatory why. It may be a notified body request or a company policy, but it isn't an MDR requirement for these devices.

## 3. What you do have to do in EUDAMED

- **Actor registration:** confirm your SRN is active and your details are current. Do the same for your authorised representative or importers if you have them.
- **UDI/device registration:** register the Basic UDI-DI and UDI-DIs for all three pumps. Devices already on the market before the mandatory date get their own transitional deadline, also about six months after it (around late November 2026). Check that date; it may be the closest deadline you face.
- **Link devices to certificates:** a Class IIb registration references the certificate covering the device. That works smoothly only once the notified body has entered the certificate. If its upload lags behind your registration, you'll hit dependencies.

## 4. Next steps

1. **Ask your notified body** when it plans to upload your certificates, and ask for the list of certificate numbers it will enter. Make sure that list matches your own register, including supplements.
2. **Check certificate data against device data** (Basic UDI-DIs, model names, scope wording) before either side submits, so the records link cleanly.
3. **Plan around the device-registration deadline,** which is probably earlier than the certificate one.
4. **Confirm the SSCP position** with regulatory and your notified body, so effort isn't spent on something the MDR doesn't require for these pumps.

I can't check live sources from here, so take the exact transitional dates from the official Commission notice or the EUDAMED site rather than from me or secondary summaries.

If your route was Annex X type-examination with Annex XI instead, check those certificates.
- **All supplements and amendments** that change scope or validity.
- **Every certificate currently valid**, including the 2023 ones if they haven't expired.

If you still sell any legacy MDD-certified devices under the Article 120 transition, tell me. Their registration rules are different and need separate checking.

1. Ask your notified body when it will upload your certificates and how it will confirm they're done.
2. Make sure your device registrations are complete and linked to those certificates. This is the part your company is responsible for.
3. Drop the SSCP work for these three pumps, unless your notified body has a specific reason to want one, or another device in your portfolio is implantable or Class III.

After that, there are catch-up periods for data that existed before the mandatory date: one period for registering devices already on the market, and a separate, longer one for notified bodies to enter certificates they had already issued. The deadline you read about is probably one of those catch-up periods, and it may not be the certificate one. Either way, it falls mainly on your notified body.

I'm not certain enough of the exact Official Journal notice date and the resulting deadlines to quote them. Please confirm them from the Commission's EUDAMED pages or with your notified body or regulatory affairs team. Your own device-registration deadline may well fall before the certificate one.

**Next steps:** confirm your SRN, get the Basic UDI-DI and UDI-DI records for all three pumps registered and correct, and ask your notified body for its timeline for entering certificates.

graders.evidence:
Two parts of your plan need correcting before the steps.

## 1. You don't upload the certificates. Your notified body does.

Under MDR Art. 56(5) and Art. 57, the notified body enters certificate information into EUDAMED's NB & Certificates module. That includes certificates issued, amended, supplemented, suspended, reinstated, withdrawn or refused. Manufacturers have no upload function for certificates.

The "May 2027" date you read probably mixes up two separate deadlines. Regulation (EU) 2024/1860 allowed EUDAMED modules to become mandatory one at a time. The first modules (actor registration, UDI/device registration, NB & certificates, market surveillance) became mandatory around late May 2026. The transition periods for data that already existed are, as I understand them:
- **Devices already on the market:** you register them within about 12 months, so roughly May 2027. This is probably where the date came from.
- **Certificates issued before that date and still valid:** the NB enters them within about 18 months, so roughly late 2027.

Check the exact dates against the Commission's EUDAMED page and the Official Journal notice. I can't confirm the current state of either from here.

## 2. You probably don't need an SSCP at all

Under MDR Art. 32, a Summary of Safety and Clinical Performance (SSCP) is required only for **implantable devices and Class III devices**. Non-implantable Class IIb infusion pumps fall outside that, so you don't have one to upload.

Where an SSCP is required, the manufacturer doesn't upload it either. It goes into the technical documentation, the NB validates it, and the NB uploads it to EUDAMED.

## What you actually need to do

1. **Actor registration:** make sure your organisation has its Single Registration Number (SRN) and that its actor data in EUDAMED is current. Also check your authorised representative's entry, if you have one.
2. **UDI/device registration:** register the Basic UDI-DI and UDI-DIs for all three pumps. This is your obligation and it's the one tied to the ~May 2027 deadline. For Class IIb devices, the device record references the certificate, so it links to the certificate data your NB enters.
3. **Coordinate with your NB:**
   - Confirm they have entered, or will enter, all three certificates, and when.
   - Check that the certificate numbers, Basic UDI-DIs and device scope in their records match yours exactly. Mismatches are the usual reason linking fails.
   - Ask whether any supplements or amendments issued since 2023 are covered too.
4. **Which certificates:** every MDR certificate covering these devices that is **still valid**, including amendments and supplements. That will be the NB's QMS certificate (Annex IX Ch. I) and/or the relevant technical documentation or type-examination certificates. Expired certificates aren't part of the transitional upload. If any of the pumps are still sold as legacy devices under old MDD certificates (extended transition under Reg. 2023/607), ask your NB how those are being handled, because that's a separate question.

To sum up: your NB owns the certificate upload, you have no SSCP obligation for these devices, and your real task before ~May 2027 is getting the devices registered and making sure your data matches your NB's.
